wallet-derivation-paths.Title: Understanding Wallet Derivation Paths
wallet-derivation-paths.Body:
Simply put, a derivation path refers to a hierarchical structure that is used to derive public keys from a private key. This hierarchical deterministic (HD) key generation is commonly used to securely manage multiple wallet accounts or addresses.

## Components of a Derivation Path

A derivation path typically consists of a series of indices or numbers that specify the path from the main private key to a particular public key in the hierarchical structure. This is represented as a string of numbers separated by slashes that look like:

*m/84’/0’/0’/0/0*

Here, “m” stands for “master key.” The rest of the path consists of the following:

*m/purpose’/coin_type’/account’/change/address_index*

## Common Derivation Paths in Leather Bitcoin Wallet

### Derivation paths for Native SegWit addresses

For Bitcoin balances, Leather uses Native SegWit addresses. This means that the derivation path for Bitcoin balances in Leather follow this format:

*m/84’/0’/0’/0/0*

The “account” number you see in the derivation path would increase based on the number of accounts associated with your wallet and private key. This means that if you were to create additional accounts, the derivation paths for the generated public keys would follow this convention:

- Account 2 would have a derivation path of: *m/84’/0’/1’/0/0*
- Account 500 would have a derivation path of: *m/84’/0’/499’/0/0*
### Derivation paths for Taproot addresses

For Ordinals-related transactions, Leather uses Taproot addresses. The derivation path associated with Taproot addresses take this structure:

*m/86’/0’/0’/0/0*

Similar to what you’d see for Native SegWit addresses, subsequent Taproot addresses that are associated with your wallet would have a different “account” number. This means that if you were to create additional accounts, the derivation paths for the generated public keys would follow this convention:

- Account 2 would have a derivation path of: *m/86’/0’/1’/0/0*
- Account 500 would have a derivation path of: *m/86’/0’/499’/0/0*
### Derivation paths for Stacks addresses

For Stacks-related assets like STX tokens, Stacks NFTs, and SIP10 tokens, Leather uses a wallet’s Stacks address. Derivation paths for Stacks addresses in Leather look like:

*m/44'/5757'/0'/0/0*

However, the derivation path for Stacks addresses in Leather differs in that the “address_index” value is what changes when users create additional accounts. This means that for Stacks addresses, the derivation paths for the generated public keys would follow this convention:

- Account 2 would have a derivation path of: *m/44'/5757'/0'/0/1*
- Account 500 would have a derivation path of: */44'/5757'/0'/0/499*
### Derivation paths for Stacks addresses in Ledger

Ledger devices will typically reveal the derivation path of existing Stacks addresses associated with a Leather wallet using the same convention outlined above.

However, the derivation paths for Stacks addresses generated by a Ledger device are different than those created by the Leather extension. In this case, the “account” value will change as users generate additional Stacks addresses with their Ledger device. This means that if you were to create additional Stacks accounts in Ledger, the derivation paths would normally follow this convention:

- Account 2 would have a derivation path of: *m/44’/5757’/1’/0/0*
- Account 500 would have a derivation path of: *m/44'/5757’/499’/0/0*
## Why are Wallet Derivation Paths Important?

Understanding wallet derivation paths is important for a number of reasons:

- **Security:** The hierarchical structure of derivation paths allows you to generate multiple public keys from a single master private key. This reduces the risk of exposure, though it’s technically very difficult to [trace different accounts back to one wallet](https://leather.io/guides/account-privacy).
- **Organization:** Derivation paths can help organize and manage multiple accounts or addresses associated with different networks.
- **Compatibility:** Following standard derivation paths ensures compatibility with various wallets and services that support HD key generation.
Overall, understanding derivation paths is crucial for effectively managing and securing your assets.

## Viewing Accounts in Other Wallets Using Derivation Paths

Knowing how to identify derivation paths can help you track different accounts associated with Leather in other wallet applications. In this case, we’ll use Sparrow as an example.

In Sparrow’s “Settings” tab, you’ll notice that the “Derivation” line under “Keystores” is filled in with a derivation path. This is the derivation path associated with the Leather wallet that you imported into Sparrow.

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/0e903b055cb2336a59d988c81af84290.png)

You can change the numbers in the “account” portion (or the “purpose” tab if you’re looking for a Taproot or Stacks address) of the wallet’s derivation path to view the address associated with a specific account you’ve created. Go to the “Addresses” tab after entering a derivation path value, and you’ll notice that the address associated with that specific Leather account will show up.

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/b36b5c06d9b6fce772d5f7b084816c26.png)

## Related Guides

- [Account privacy](https://leather.io/guides/account-privacy)
- [Add or restore accounts](https://leather.io/guides/add-or-restore-accounts)
- [Understanding Bitcoin address types](https://leather.io/guides/bitcoin-address-types)

leather-luminex.Title: How to Use Leather on Luminex
leather-luminex.Body:
Luminex is an Ordinals launchpad that gives users the ability to mint inscriptions and Runes. It also gives Leather Bitcoin wallet users [snapshots of the Runes market](https://luminex.io/runes/alpha) for them to determine which Runes tokens they might want to mint, and access to Runes trading on Magic Eden.

## How to Connect to Luminex with Leather

To connect to Luminex using your Leather wallet:

1. Go to [luminex.io](http://luminex.io/) and click “Login” on the top right
1. Select “Leather” from the wallet options that appear and click “Connect Leather” in the Leather pop-up window to continue
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/11daaa0cc66880d7e6b20b74f158f4e5.png)

## How to Mint Ordinals in Luminex with Leather

To mint Ordinals in Luminex using your Leather wallet:

1. Click “Mint Ordinals,” which will take you to the Luminex Minter
1. Enter your inscription information or attach files you’d like to inscribe in the “Inscription Info” section
1. Double check that the Taproot address associated with your wallet has been entered in the “Receiver Address” field under the “Confirm Mint” section
1. Select your fee option and click “Mint”
1. Confirm the transaction in the Leather pop-up window that appears
1. You inscription should appear in the “Collectibles” section of your Leather wallet once the transaction has been confirmed
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/82b74623d40538ea9ccb01fffc2f74c2.png)

## How to Inscribe Ordinals On Rare Sats in Luminex with Leather

If you want to inscribe your Ordinal on rare sats in Luminex:

1. Once you’ve completed the “Inscription Info” section for your mint, proceed to the “Rare Sats” section
1. Select the rare sat you’d like to inscribe on
1. If you need to buy a rare sat, click on the “Buy” tab to view rare sats that are available and click the “Purchase” button once you have selected rare sats to buy; click “Confirm” to finish the transaction in Leather
1. Double check that the Taproot address associated with your wallet has been entered in the “Receiver Address” field under the “Confirm Mint” section
1. Select your fee option and click “Mint”
1. Confirm the transaction in the Leather pop-up window that appears
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/5a8d85ac36682af9877bdad8f3941d85.png)

## How to Mint Parent-Child Inscriptions in Luminex with Leather

If you want to mint parent-child inscriptions in Luminex:

1. Once you’ve completed the “Inscription Info” section for your mint, proceed to the “Parent/Child” section and click on the dropdown
1. Enter the inscription ID of the parent inscription
1. Double check that the Taproot address associated with your wallet has been entered in the “Receiver Address” field under the “Confirm Mint” section
1. Select your fee option and click “Mint”
1. Confirm the transaction in the Leather pop-up window that appears
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/42874e01629cc06c22f398d55d75125c.png)

## How to Reinscribe Ordinals in Luminex with Leather

If you want to reinscribe Ordinals in Luminex: 

1. Once you’ve completed the “Inscription Info” section for your mint, proceed to the “Reinscription” section and click on the dropdown
1. Enter the inscription ID or the UTXO location to inscribe on
1. Double check that the Taproot address associated with your wallet has been entered in the “Receiver Address” field under the “Confirm Mint” section
1. Select your fee option and click “Mint”
1. Confirm the transaction in the Leather pop-up window that appears
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/fcb08a3b65ba57cdcad5f1b5e8bf1899.png)

## How to Mint Bitcoin Runes in Luminex with Leather

To mint existing Runes tokens in Luminex: 

1. Click “Mint Runes,” which will take you to the Luminex Runes dashboard
1. Select the Runes token you’d like to mint by clicking “Mint”
1. Enter how many tokens you’d like for a “Repeat Mint” 
1. Select the “Minting Mode” option that you’d like to use
1. Select the fee option for your transaction
1. Click “Mint”
1. Confirm the transaction in the Leather pop-up window that appears
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/ec98ee9fc22694c7f3ce0963dcc6b863.png)

## How to Etch Runes in Luminex with Leather

Users who want to create their own Runes tokens will need to etch a Rune. To etch a Rune in Luminex:

1. Select the “Etch” tab in the Luminex Runes dashboard
1. Enter the Rune ticker info
1. Determine how many decimals you’d like your Runes token to display along with its symbol
1. Determine the “Max Supply” of the Runes token
1. Enter a number to determine the “Limit per Mint” for the token
1. Choose your fee option and click “Submit Etch”
1. Confirm the transaction in the Leather pop-up window that appears
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/4d809aeda704a93463ea084e45b5fb6f.png)

## How to Transfer Runes in Luminex with Leather

To transfer Runes in Luminex with Leather: 

1. Select the “Transfer” tab in the Luminex Runes dashboard
1. Select the Runes you want to transfer
1. Enter a value in “Amount to Transfer” 
1. Enter the recipient’s address in “Receiver Address”
1. You can choose to “Split Runes” and enter the number of UTXOs you’d like for this particular transfer
1. Select your fee option
1. Click “Transfer” and confirm the transaction in the Leather pop-up window that appears
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/de449073ec4dc861989b04f484eb6116.png)

leather-ordinalsbot.Title: How to Use Leather on OrdinalsBot
leather-ordinalsbot.Body:
OrdinalsBot was one of the earliest platforms that allowed users to inscribe Ordinals. Today, it is still one of the most user-friendly Ordinals launchpads. 

Leather users can connect to OrdinalsBot to mint Ordinals and Runes, conduct additional transactions with BRC-20 tokens, and more.

## How to Connect to OrdinalsBot with Leather

To connect to OrdinalsBot using your Leather wallet:

1. Go to [OrdinalsBot.com](http://ordinalsbot.com/) and click “Connect” on the top right
1. Select “Leather Wallet” from the wallet options that appear and click “Connect Leather” in the Leather pop-up window to continue
Click “Sign” in the Leather pop-up window to finishing connecting to OrdinalsBot

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/5419d0fe57056655bbd6c89fc81395fd.png)

## How to Mint Ordinals in OrdinalsBot with Leather

To mint Ordinals in OrdinalsBot using your Leather wallet:

1. Upload the file you want to inscribe on the OrdinalsBot homepage, or click the “Text” tab to inscribe text
1. Check the “Optimize images” box to further prepare your image file for the inscription
1. Select the specific satoshi type you’d like to inscribe on
1. Select the fee option for your transaction
1. Click “Submit & pay invoice”
1. In the “Pay with Wallet” tab, select “Pay with Connected Wallet”
1. Click “Continue” in the Leather pop-up window that appears
1. Check your transaction fee option and click “Send” to complete the transaction in Leather
## How to Mint BRC-20 Tokens in OrdinalsBot with Leather

OrdinalsBot also makes it easy for Leather users to mint and deploy their BRC-20 tokens. Users should remember minting a BRC-20 token is a two-step process which involves minting and then deploying the token. 

To mint a transfer inscription for a BRC-20 token in OrdinalsBot:

1. Select the “Brc20” tab and make sure “Mint” is selected
1. Enter the 4-letter ticker for your BRC-20 token as well as the amount you’d like to mint and repeat amount
1. Select the rare sat you’d like to inscribe on and click "Next"
1. Double check the JSON data that appears
1. Select the fee option you’d like for your mint and click “Submit & pay invoice”
1. In the “Pay with Wallet” tab, select “Pay with Connected Wallet”
1. Click “Continue” in the Leather pop-up window that appears
1. Check your transaction fee option and click “Send” to complete the transaction in Leather
1. The transfer inscription associated with your mint should appear in the “Collectibles” section of your wallet once the transaction has been confirmed
## How to Deploy BRC-20 Tokens in OrdinalsBot with Leather

To deploy a BRC-20 token using a transfer inscription on OrdinalsBot: 

1. Select the “Brc20” tab and make sure “Deploy” is selected
1. Enter the BRC-20 token’s ticker and set the total token supply and limit that can be created per mint and click “Next”
1.  Double check the JSON data that appears
1. Select the fee option you’d like for the deployment and click “Submit & pay invoice”
1. In the “Pay with Wallet” tab, select “Pay with Connected Wallet”
1. Click “Continue” in the Leather pop-up window that appears
1. Check your transaction fee option and click “Send” to complete the transaction in Leather
## How to Etch Bitcoin Runes in OrdinalsBot with Leather

OrdinalsBot allows Leather users to mint and etch Bitcoin Runes tokens. To etch Runes on OrdinalsBot:

1. Click the “Runes” tab on the OrdinalsBot homepage
1. Make sure that the “Etch” tab is selected and enter the ticker, supply, and all the fields needed to provide details about your Runes token and click "Next"
1. Double check your Runes etching details before clicking “Next”
1. Select the fee option you’d like and click “Submit & pay invoice”
1. In the “Pay with Wallet” tab, select “Pay with Connected Wallet”
1. Click “Continue” in the Leather pop-up window that appears
1. Check your transaction fee option and click “Send” to complete the transaction in Leather
## How to Mint Runes in Luminex with Leather

Users who want to mint Runes in OrdinalsBot will need to:

1. Select the “Mint” tab in the OrdinalsBot’s Runes dashboard
1. Enter the ticker for an existing Rune token and number of mints
1. Select the fee option you’d like and click “Submit & pay invoice”
1. In the “Pay with Wallet” tab, select “Pay with Connected Wallet”
1. Click “Continue” in the Leather pop-up window that appears
1. Check your transaction fee option and click “Send” to complete the transaction in Leather

connect-ledger.Title: Connect Leather with Your Ledger Hardware Wallet
connect-ledger.Body:
For added security, users may opt to connect their Leather extension with a cold wallet storage option. 

Ledger devices are compatible with the Leather extension and give users another option for managing their tokens and collectibles.

## How to Set Up Your Ledger Device

When you connect your Ledger device to your computer, a series of steps will appear on your device’s screen to help you complete the setup process. Make sure that you have downloaded the Ledger Live app to proceed.

The next steps will require you to take action on both your hardware device and the Ledger Live app. 

To set up your Ledger wallet:

1. Plug your Leather device into your computer
1. Select the Ledger device that you’re using
1. If this is your first time setting up your Ledger device, select the “Setup a new [insert device name]” option on the page that appears
1. Set up a pin by following the instructions that appear on your Ledger device before clicking “Next step” in the Ledger Live app
1. Record the 24-word recovery phrase displayed on your Ledger device to proceed
1. Download the Ledger Live “Bitcoin (BTC)” app or the “Stacks (STX)” app
1. Select “Add account” to create your first Bitcoin account
## How to Connect Your Ledger Device with Leather

To connect your Ledger device to the Leather extension, you’ll need to do so via the installation homepage that appears when you install the Leather extension for the first time. This might require you to uninstall and reinstall the extension, which is why we emphasize that users properly secure their Secret Keys.

To connect your existing Ledger device with Leather:

1. Select the “Use Ledger” option from the installation homepage
1. Unlock your Ledger device
1. Ensure that your Ledger device is connected to the “Bitcoin (BTC)” or “Stacks (STX)” app
1. Click “Connect Bitcoin” 
1. Select your Ledger device from the list of compatible devices that appear and click “Connect”

integrated-swap-disabled.Body:

In these cases, please check back in a few days or use another (decentralized) exchange to make the swap instead.

increase-fee.Title: Increase Transaction Fee
increase-fee.Body:
Increased activity on the Bitcoin network could mean that your transactions will take longer to process. That’s why users have the option of increasing fees to ensure that their transactions process more quickly.

## How to Increase Transaction Fees with Leather

1. Click on the “Activity” tab in your Leather extension
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/7b4c06532023a30a8bf15da79737c56d.png)

1. Select the “Increase fee” option on the specific transaction you’d like to increase the fee for
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/5d9f3fd1a2f4a1c2a56be338e34caed2.png)

1. Select the fee increase you’d like to make for your transaction
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/de5f52b78da48e251722a6e44cc767b1.png)

## Related Guides

- [Configure transaction fees](leather.io/guides/configure-transaction-fees)

migrating-ordinals-sparrow-leather.Title: Migrating Ordinals to Leather from Sparrow
migrating-ordinals-sparrow-leather.Body:
Users often want to transfer their Ordinals from one wallet to another. This guide will help Sparrow users migrate their Ordinals collections to Leather. 

## How to Transfer Your Ordinals Collection From Sparrow into Leather

1. Open the “Settings” tab of your Sparrow Wallet and click “View Seed”. Copy your seed phrase.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/b824f597fb3563836c9f94546eb49ca1.png)

1. Install the[ Leather extension](https://leather.io/install-extension).
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/986599894670766b001c8c226746aad6.png)

1. Select “Use existing key” when you reach the extension home page.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/68f07b58453709b161e885ec9cf0e11c.png)

1. Enter the seed phrase you copied from your Sparrow Wallet into the Secret Key input form. 
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/7421608f42ffe222b204a27868d294f7.png)

1. Your Ordinals will be displayed in the “Collectibles” section of your Leather home page.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/c73e99a2bc89acedf63f2fcf33163171.png)

By following these steps, you should be able to migrate all of your Ordinals at once. If you experience any difficulties or have any questions during this process, please contact [support@leather.io](mailto:support@leather.io).

receive-assets.Title: Receive Assets
receive-assets.Body:
Sending and receiving assets is one of the most basic functions of any crypto wallet. Leather gives users the ability to easily receive Bitcoin-backed assets from other wallet accounts and users.

## How to Receive Assets in Leather

1. Determine which type of asset (token or collectible) you’ll be receiving
1. Based on the type of asset you’re receiving, determine which Bitcoin address you’ll need for the transaction
1. Hit the “Receive” button in the main menu of your extension
1. Select “Tokens” or “Collectibles” to view the addresses you’ll need
1. Copy the appropriate address for the asset you’re looking to receive
1. Paste and send your address to the intended sender
<video src="https://youtu.be/utH1rI6fQCg"></video>

Once the transaction has been confirmed by the Bitcoin network, the assets you received will be displayed under the “Assets” tab on your main Leather extension page.

## Related Guides

- [Receive Tokens](leather.io/guides/receive-tokens)
- [Receive Collectibles](leather.io/guides/receive-collectibles)
- [Receive Bitcoin (BTC)](leather.io/guides/receive-btc)

receive-assets.Sentence: Here's how Leather users can receive assets in-app.
receive-assets.Summary: Sending and receiving assets is a fundamental function of any crypto wallet, and Leather makes it simple for users to receive Bitcoin-backed assets from other wallet accounts and users. By following a few easy steps, users can securely receive the assets they desire within the Leather platform. # How to Receive Bitcoin Stamps Using Leather

pending-transactions.Title: Understand Pending Transactions
pending-transactions.Body:
It is common for users to wait anywhere from 2 to 60 minutes for a transaction confirmation. However, if your transaction has been pending for more than 2 hours, this usually indicates that traffic on the network is high and fees have increased.

In these cases, your transaction may be dropped after a certain amount of blocks or amount of time has passed. While unconfirmed transactions have no impact on a user’s wallet (the transaction never went through), users can take steps to increase the likelihood of their transactions being processed promptly.

## How to Troubleshoot Pending Transactions in Leather

If your transaction has been pending for several hours, open your Leather extension and check that:

### You have enough funds for the transaction

Every transaction requires the user to pay a fee on top of the original transaction balance. Paying higher fees during peak network traffic incentivizes miners to confirm your transaction promptly in upcoming blocks.

A transaction could remain unconfirmed for hours if a user does not have the funds needed to cover both the transaction and the associated fee. If that is the case, you can fund your wallet and re-send the transaction if it ends up being dropped.

### You’re able to reconfigure the transaction fee

Additionally, you can reconfigure the fee associated with your transaction. If your transaction has been pending for a while, selecting a higher fee will often increase the chances of your transaction being confirmed in the next block.

After making sure that you have enough funds to cover a fee increase, click on your transaction in the “Activity” tab and follow these steps.

### There are no nonce gaps

Stacks transactions in Leather use nonces to determine what order transactions are processed. These nonces are processed sequentially, meaning that a Leather account that hasn’t sent any transactions will begin at nonce 0, and subsequent transactions will be automatically set at 1, 2, 3, etc. Transaction nonces can be viewed on the [Stacks Explorer](https://explorer.hiro.so/transactions?chain=mainnet).

If there are gaps in the nonces associated with your account (going from 30 to 32, for example), you’ll want to edit your nonce to make sure that it matches the sequence order. You can also send a completely new transaction, edit the nonce to be similar to that of a pending transaction, and set a higher fee to replace the pending transaction with your preferred nonce.

Please note that it does take time for transactions to propagate over the network, and transactions with a higher fee will replace those with a lower fee even if they share the same nonce.

## Related Guides

- [Increase transaction fee](leather.io/guides/increase-fee)
- [Configure transaction fee](leather.io/guides/configure-transaction-fees)
- [Configure transaction nonces](leather.io/guides/configure-transaction-nonces)

send-stx.Title: Send STX Tokens
send-stx.Body:
# Send STX Tokens with Leather

In addition to sending Bitcoin (BTC), Leather allows you to send Stacks (STX) to other wallets and accounts. Here’s how to send STX quickly and securely:

## How to Send STX Tokens in Leather

1. **Open Leather**: From your Leather Wallet home screen, click **Send**.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/3ef521e9431b5cd4b64b71fba41874cb.png)

1. **Select Stacks (STX)**: Choose **Stacks (STX)** as the asset you want to send.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/90743f8d4ad513a45191ebbe0801590d.png)

1. **Enter the Transaction Details****Amount**: Specify how much STX you want to send.**Recipient’s Address**: Paste the receiving wallet’s STX address. Alternatively, select the BNS Name option via the dropdown menu and add a BNS name. The corresponding Stacks address will be checked, and the transfer will be sent there. **Memo (Optional)**: Typically, a memo is not required when sending STX to a non-custodial wallet. However, some exchanges require a memo for proper crediting—if you’re sending STX to an exchange, check their deposit instructions.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/1ab7d85c488801817a6b517a8c603565.png)

1. **Choose Your Fee**: Select a fee option based on how quickly you want the transaction confirmed. **Standard** is typically sufficient. **Custom **is for advanced users.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/3844442516005ba1dc8763b04848507e.png)

1. **Review and Confirm**: Double-check the amount, address, and fee. When ready, click **Send** to broadcast your STX transaction to the network.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/cfbb2d0147ea2805ba72c322c233019b.png)

**Tip**: Always verify the recipient’s STX address. Sending tokens to an incompatible or incorrect address can result in permanent loss.

# How to Buy Stacks (STX) Tokens for Use with Leather

This guide focuses on buying Stacks (STX) using centralized exchanges, the Leather “Buy” feature, and decentralized options. Users can purchase STX to fund their Leather Wallet for use within the Stacks Ecosystem. The process mirrors buying and depositing Bitcoin (BTC) through various exchanges.

## Where Can I Buy STX?

Leather users can choose from a variety of centralized exchanges to buy STX. Here are some popular options:

- **Coinbase**: Available in the US and internationally, fast checkout
- **MoonPay**: Available in the US and internationally, fast checkout
- **Transak**: Available in the US and internationally, fast checkout
- **Binance**: Available in the US and internationally
- **Blockchain.com**: Available in the US and internationally
- **Bybit**: Available only outside of the US
- **Crypto.com**: Available in the US and internationally
- **Gate.io**: Available only outside of the US
- **KuCoin**: Available only outside of the US
- **OKX**: Available only outside of the US
Most exchanges require you to create an account with a valid email and complete Know Your Customer (KYC) verification before trading.

## Buy STX with Leather via a Central Exchange (Fast Checkout)

Leather provides a Fast Checkout option with select exchanges. This method automatically sends STX directly to your Leather Wallet without an extra deposit step. To use Fast Checkout:

1. **Open Leather**: Click the “Buy” button on your main account page.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/773c3f1a25d582a8b81c319d77b5ee59.png)

1. **Select Stacks**: Choose Stacks (STX) when prompted.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/49f6a58549e1c74f2301a13d381ee6ce.png)

1. **Pick a Fast Checkout Exchange**: Select an exchange marked with “Fast Checkout” to purchase STX directly with a credit card.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/f6e766aaa8626082a7261693529192c4.png)

1. **Complete the Purchase**: Follow the exchange prompts to finalize your STX purchase.
**Note**: With Fast Checkout, your STX is automatically sent to your Leather Wallet—no additional steps are needed.

## Buy at a Central Exchange and Deposit in Leather

If you’re not using a Fast Checkout exchange, follow these steps to buy STX on a central exchange and then deposit it into your Leather Wallet:

1. **Create an Exchange Account**: Register with your chosen exchange and complete any required KYC steps.
1. **Purchase STX**: Use your preferred payment method to buy Stacks (STX) on the exchange.
1. **Get Your Stacks Address**: Open Leather, click “Receive,” and copy your Stacks address.
1. **Send STX from the Exchange**: In the exchange interface, choose to Send or Withdraw STX.
1. **Paste Your Wallet Address**: Enter the Stacks address you copied from Leather as the recipient.
1. **Confirm and Send**: Double-check the address and confirm the withdrawal. Your STX should appear in your Leather Wallet within a few minutes (delays are possible due to high network traffic).
Always verify that you’re depositing STX to a compatible address, and double-check transaction details before finalizing.

Exchanges that are labeled with “Fast checkout” will let you purchase and deposit your tokens with a credit card.

## Non-Custodial and Decentralized Options

For users interested in non-custodial or decentralized methods to acquire STX, alternative flows exist—though they may require additional steps:

### Option 1: Swap BTC for STX (BRC-20) on Bitcoin L1

1. Use[ Alex Lab’s Bitcoin Swap](https://app.alexlab.co/bitcoin/swap) to convert BTC to STX (BRC-20) on Bitcoin Layer 1.
1. Then, use[ Xlink Network](https://app.xlink.network/) to bridge your STX (BRC-20) from Bitcoin L1 to the Stacks (Bitcoin L2) network.
### 

### Option 2: Peg BTC to sBTC and Swap for STX

1. When available, peg BTC to sBTC using Leather.
1. Then use[ Alex Lab’s Swap](https://app.alexlab.co/swap) with a sponsored transaction to convert some sBTC to STX.
## 

## What You Can Do With STX and Leather

Once you have STX in your Leather Wallet, you can explore the full range of activities on the Stacks network, which extends Bitcoin’s functionality with smart contracts and decentralized apps (dApps). You can interact with DeFi protocols, mint or trade NFTs, and even lock your STX in “Stacking” to help secure the network while potentially earning BTC rewards. 

You can also connect your Leather Wallet to various Stacks-powered platforms to participate in governance, play blockchain-based games, and more—making STX a versatile asset for users looking to leverage Bitcoin’s security with the flexibility of smart contracts.Related Guides

##

send-bitcoin.Title: Send Bitcoin (BTC)
send-bitcoin.Body:
# Send Bitcoin (BTC)

## How to Send Bitcoin in Leather

Sending BTC to other wallets (yours or someone else’s) is one of the core functions of Leather. Follow these steps to send Bitcoin quickly, securely, and efficiently.

1. From your Leather Wallet home screen, click or tap the **Send** button.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/3ef521e9431b5cd4b64b71fba41874cb.png)

1. When prompted to choose an asset, select Bitcoin (BTC).
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/53db2cd5e8b26164c4a57ec0348441d2.png)

1. Enter Transaction Details**Amount**: Specify how much BTC you want to send.**Recipient’s Address**: Paste or type the Bitcoin address you wish to send to. Double-check the address carefully to avoid errors. Whenever possible, paste the address.Press **Continue** when you’re ready.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/7f86acf5b3c6c266d1ef24bfebaad87f.png)

1. **Choose Your Fee**: Leather gives you control over the transaction fee.**Standard Fee**: A balanced option for most transactions.**Priority Fee**: Opt for a higher fee if you want faster confirmation.**Custom Fee**: For advanced users who want to set a precise fee.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/c486a4c4c68c85329ec3fb3ab4055cb2.png)

1. **Review and Confirm**: Before finalizing your transaction, carefully review the Recipient’s Address, BTC Amount, and Selected Fee.
1. Once everything looks correct, click **Continue** (or **Send**) to confirm.
![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/f352a985a40ccbee00bc939927bdff3a.png)

Leather will then broadcast your transaction to the Bitcoin network. You can review the transaction in the **Activity** section of your wallet.

Read more about [pending transactions](https://leather.io/guides/pending-transactions).

## Important Reminders when Sending Bitcoin with Leather

- **Sufficient Balance**: Ensure you have enough BTC in your wallet to cover both the amount sent and the transaction fee.
- **Address Accuracy**: Bitcoin transactions are irreversible. Double-check the recipient’s address and the amount before sending, and always paste the address when possible.
- **Keep Your Wallet Secure**: If you need help backing up or restoring your wallet, refer to our [Guides](https://leather.io/guides). We recommend keeping physical backups of your secret keys (seed phrases) in separate, secure locations.
By following these steps, you can ensure a smooth experience when sending Bitcoin from your Leather Wallet. If you have any further questions or encounter any issues, don’t hesitate to consult our [Support Center](https://leather.io/contact).

## Related Guides

- [Buy bitcoin (BTC)](leather.io/guides/buy-bitcoin)
- [Send STX tokens ](leather.io/guides/send-stx)

bitcoin-address-types.Title: Understand Bitcoin Address Types
bitcoin-address-types.Body:
Bitcoin addresses are alphanumeric identifiers used to conduct transactions on the Bitcoin blockchain. There are several types of Bitcoin addresses – each with its own unique format and characteristics – that correspond to different types of Bitcoin transactions.

This guide will help you identify different Bitcoin address types and determine which address to use depending on the transaction type.

## Types of Bitcoin Addresses

The most commonly used Bitcoin address types are:

### Legacy Addresses

- The original Bitcoin address type that is compatible with all Bitcoin wallets and exchanges
- Start with the number “1”
- Offer a high level of compatibility, though they do take up more space on the blockchain
### Segregated Witness Addresses (SegWit)

- Start with the characters “3”
- Supported by most modern Bitcoin wallets and exchanges
- Offer improved efficiency compared to legacy addresses
### Native SegWit Addresses (Bech32)

- Start with the characters “bc1q”
- Supported by some Bitcoin wallets like Leather
### Stacks Addresses

- Start with the letter “S”
- Supported by Stacks wallets like Leather and can be employed for Stacked-based transactions
### Taproot Addresses

- Start with the characters “bc1p”
- Supported by certain Bitcoin wallets like Leather and are frequently used for transactions involving assets that make use of Taproot, such as Ordinals and BRC-20 tokens
## How to Find Bitcoin Address Types in Leather

Leather automatically generates Bitcoin addresses for you when you create your wallet. You can view all address types associated with your wallet by clicking the “Receive” button on your wallet home screen.

You’ll find each type of Bitcoin address listed with the corresponding asset type it’s intended for (eg. your Taproot address for Ordinals). Therefore, the “Receive” page serves as a dependable reference for identifying the address types to use for various transactions, whether you’re looking to buy, send, receive, or swap a token or collectible.

secure-secret-key.Title: Secure Your Secret Key
secure-secret-key.Body:
When users create a Leather wallet, a 24-word phrase is generated. This phrase is known as a Secret Key, and users need to make sure to store this Secret Key in a place that only they can access. 

## What is a Secret Key?

Secret Keys are more conventionally known as “seed phrases,” mnemonic seed phrases,” “recovery seeds,” or “recovery phrases.” They’re essentially randomly generated cryptographic keys that protect a user’s crypto wallet and, consequently, the assets held within the wallet.

Secret Keys generated by Leather are BIP39-compatible and in English. Technically, you can check to see if your Secret Key is compatible by cross-checking all of the generated words against [this list](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0039/english.txt). If you’re having trouble entering your Secret Key when prompted to do so, please double check that:

- All words are lowercase
- Words are separated by only one space
- You haven’t entered any numbers or special characters
### Secret Keys vs. Passwords

While users may think of Secret Keys as a password of sorts, it’s important to distinguish between the two. 

Passwords are unique to each device and are created by the user to access their wallet on a particular browser or computer. They are helpful if you use the same device and browser to access your Leather wallet, as they save you from having to re-enter your Secret Key every time you log in.

Unlike Secret Keys, passwords can be reset and easily recovered. While there is a way to recover your Secret Key using backup data from your computer, a Secret Key is generally extremely difficult to recover once lost. It is crucial for users to keep a copy of their Secret Key in a very secure location that only they have access to. 

You will often be prompted for your Secret Key if you attempt to log into your wallet from a computer or browser that you don’t normally use, or if you previously signed out from your wallet. That’s why it’s important to make sure that you back up your Secret Key the moment it is revealed to you. You do have the ability to view your Secret Key from within the extension, but that’s provided that you can already access your wallet. 

## How to Secure Your Secret Key with Leather

The Cryptocurrency Security Standard (CCSS) offers [guidelines](https://cryptoconsortium.org/cryptocurrency-security-standard-documentation/details/) for user key storage. These guidelines are ordered from the least secure (Level I) to most secure (Level III). 

We recommend that users adhere to the CCSS’ Level II standards at the very least. This involves:

- Backing up each of your cryptographic keys separately 
- Storing the backup in a different location from where you access your wallet (e.g. if you access your wallet from a computer located in your office, you may want to store your Secret Key in another room)
- Storing your backup in a location that minimizes possible access by unauthorized parties (e.g. a safe or lock box)
- Employing a tamper mechanism that helps you determine if your backup was accessed by another party
Please note that we do not store our users’ Secret Keys, nor can we help our users recover their Secret Keys should they become lost. Leather is a self-custodied Bitcoin wallet, which means that users, alone, are responsible for their keys.

This also means that if your Secret Key has been stolen by harmful websites or software, there are no guarantees that you will be able to recover your wallet assets. Consequently, we ask that users think twice before revealing or entering their Secret Key in another application besides Leather.

create-new-wallet.Body:
This guide is specifically for users who are creating an entirely new Leather wallet. If you have an existing Leather wallet that you’d like to access in a new browser, please visit our “Accessing an existing wallet” guide.

## How to Create a New Leather Bitcoin Wallet

1. Open your Leather wallet browser extension
1. Hit “Allow” when asked for permission to give Leather access to deidentified service usage data
1. Click on “Create new wallet”
1. Copy and store your 24-word Secret Key, then click “I’ve backed it up”
1. Set a password and click “Continue"

install-leather-source.Title: Install Leather From a Source
install-leather-source.Body:
Leather has not been available in the Firefox store since November 2023. This means that Firefox users will need to install the Leather extension with the wallet’s source code if they want to access the Leather app.

Chrome, Brave, and Edge users also have the option of installing the Leather extension from a source should they prefer to do so by following these steps:

## How to Install Leather from a Source for Chrome, Brave, and Edge

1. Visit the [Leather extension Github repository](https://github.com/leather-wallet/extension) and look for the “Releases” section in the column on the right
1. Download the leather-chromium .zip file that corresponds to the latest release
1. Go to: chrome://extensions
1. Toggle on "Developer mode"
1. Click on "Load unpacked" located under the “Extensions” heading on the top left of the page
1. Select the new directory that was unpacked from the .zip file to follow the remaining extension installation steps
## How to Install Leather from a Source for Firefox

1. Visit the [Leather extension Github repository](https://github.com/leather-wallet/extension) and look for the “Releases” section in the column on the right
1. Download the leather-firefox .zip file that corresponds to the latest release
1. Open your Firefox browser and go to about:debugging
1. Click on "This Firefox"
1. Click on "Load Temporary Add-on…"
1. Open the new directory that was unpacked from the .zip file and select “manifest.json”
1. Follow the remaining extension installation steps
**Note:** Unlike installations from [the Chrome Web Store](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/stacks-wallet/ldinpeekobnhjjdofggfgjlcehhmanlj), installing Leather from the source code does *not* allow the app to automatically update to newer versions. You will need to reinstall the extension using the steps outlined above when newer releases become available.

## Related Guides

- [Install Leather](https://leather.io/guides/install-leather)
- [Install Leather desktop wallet](https://leather.io/guides/install-desktop-bitcoin-wallet)
- [Install Leather for developer builders](https://leather.io/guides/install-leather-developers)

install-leather-developers.Title: Install Leather for developer builds
install-leather-developers.Body:
When Leather developers have finished building a new feature or bug fix, they will often create a new version of the Chrome extension for testing purposes prior to public release. These versions give users the opportunity to try new wallet features and point out areas for improvement.

## How to Install Leather for Developer Builds

1. Find the specific [pull request on Github](https://github.com/leather-wallet/extension/pulls) with the feature or fix you’d like to test
1. Download the extension by clicking on the “Extension build” link in the first line of the pull request
1. Scroll down and click on the wallet version under “Artifacts” and unzip the extension build when prompted.
1. Go to “chrome://extensions” to turn off your current Leather extension
1. Switch on “Developer mode” at the top right corner of the extension management page
1. Click the “Load unpacked” button that should appear underneath the “Extensions” tab on the upper left corner of the page
1. Select the folder you downloaded that houses the unzipped wallet extension
1. Depending on the feature you’re looking to test, you will either restore the wallet with an existing Secret Key, or you’ll create a new wallet for the purposes of the test
1. Test the new feature or fix
Following the test, you can submit your results and share your experience by returning to the specific Github pull request. You’ll see a “Test report” link next to the initial “Extension build” link that you clicked.

## Related Guides

- [Create a new wallet](leather.io/guides/create-new-wallet)
- [Change network](leather.io/guides/change-network)
- [Obtain STX tokens for testnet](leather.io/guides/obtain-testnet-stx)

Installing a developer build of Leather lets contributors test unreleased features or debug changes in local environments. This is particularly helpful when contributing to Leather or integrating API methods still under development.

The process involves downloading the zipped build artifact, extracting its contents, and manually loading it as an unpacked extension in your Chromium-based browser such as Chrome, Brave, or Edge.

bridge-sbtc.Title: Bridge BTC to sBTC
bridge-sbtc.Body:
Leather users can bridge their BTC to sBTC in-app using the swap function (a minimum of 0.01 BTC is required). Users who obtain sBTC can then enroll their asset as part of the rewards program run by Bitcoin L2 Labs. 

Users should note that there are two transaction fees required to mint your sBTC. The first is manually set by the user when initiating the deposit transaction within their wallet. The second is a fee used to consolidate the deposit UTXOs into a single signer UTXO. This separate transaction fee happens automatically and is set to a max of 80k sats, which is also automatically deducted from your minted sBTC. 

This is not a minting fee but a regular Bitcoin transaction fee labeled as "Max Signer Fee" in Leather.

## How to Bridge BTC to sBTC in Leather

1. Click on “Swap”
1. In the “You’ll pay” dropdown, select “Bitcoin” and determine the amount of BTC you’d like to bridge
1. In the “You’ll receive” dropdown, select “sBTC”
1. Click “Review and Bridge”
1. Double check the transaction confirmation details and click “Bridge”
1. The sBTC you obtain will appear in the “Tokens” section of your wallet homepage once the transaction has been confirmed

how-to-view-ledger-live-stx-funds-in.Title: How to View Ledger Live STX Funds in Leather Wallet
how-to-view-ledger-live-stx-funds-in.Body:
*Alternative question:* I can’t find funds (i.e. STX, BTC) displayed in Ledger Live when I try to access it with the Ledger device in Leather, why is that?

If you're using a Ledger device and trying to view your Stacks (STX) funds in Leather wallet, you may encounter some compatibility challenges. This guide explains why these issues occur, how to resolve them, and provides important details about Bitcoin addresses and their differences.

## **Why Your Ledger Live Stacks Account Funds May Not Appear in Leather**

### **Derivation Path Differences**

Ledger Live and Leather Wallet use different derivation paths to generate Stacks addresses:

- Ledger Live:Account 1: m/44'/5757'/0'/0/0Account 2: m/44'/5757'/1'/0/0Account 3: m/44'/5757'/2'/0/0Additional addresses within an account: m/44'/5757'/0'/0/1, m/44'/5757'/0'/0/2, etc.
- Leather Wallet:Account 1: m/44'/5757'/0'/0/0Account 2: m/44'/5757'/0'/0/1Account 3: m/44'/5757'/0'/0/2
This means that if you generate accounts or addresses using Ledger Live, they may not align with the paths used by Leather Wallet. As a result, you may not see these addresses in Leather.

### **Fresh Address Generation in Ledger Live**

Ledger Live generates fresh addresses within an account as you use them. For example:

- The first Bitcoin address in Account 1 is always the same (m/44'/0'/0'/0/0), but subsequent addresses like m/44'/0'/0'/0/1, m/44'/0'/0'/0/2 are generated dynamically.
Leather Wallet, on the other hand, does not automatically generate new addresses beyond the initial ones. This difference affects both Bitcoin and Stacks accounts.

## **Resolving Compatibility Issues**

### **Stacks (STX)**

If your Stacks account is not appearing in Leather, here’s how to fix it:

1. **Identify the Address in Ledger Live:** Check the address in Ledger Live where your STX is stored.
1. **Send Funds to Leather’s Address:** In Leather, click "Receive" to display your Stacks address. Send your STX from the Ledger Live address to the address shown in Leather.
1. **Monitor in Ledger Live:** Once your STX balance appears in Leather, you can add this account to Ledger Live (via "Add Account") for monitoring purposes. Note that this only works if the address has a balance.
### **Bitcoin (BTC)**

For Bitcoin, the process is similar, but there are additional considerations:

- **Taproot Addresses:** Taproot addresses (used for ordinal inscriptions or collectibles) require special handling. Sending or spending BTC tied to an ordinal inscription could inadvertently destroy the collectible.
- **Separate Devices:** If you manage collectibles or inscriptions, consider using separate Ledger devices for Ledger Live and Leather accounts. This minimizes risks of accidental spending.
## **Key Differences for Bitcoin Addresses**

1. **Fresh Address Generation:**Ledger Live generates a new address once a previously generated address has been used.Leather Wallet currently does not generate new addresses automatically.
1. **Ordinal Collectibles (Taproot):**Sending BTC tied to an ordinal inscription from Ledger Live could destroy the collectible.Always double-check before sending BTC from a Taproot address.
## **Best Practices**

- **Use Leather for STX:** Always generate Stacks addresses using Leather if you plan to use the funds there. Avoid generating Stacks addresses in Ledger Live.
- **Monitor Balances with Ledger Live:** After transferring STX to a Leather address, you can monitor the balance in Ledger Live.
- **Be Cautious with Taproot Addresses:** For users holding Bitcoin collectibles, avoid accessing these accounts in Ledger Live to prevent accidental spending.
- **Separate Devices (Optional):** Consider using one Ledger device for Leather accounts and another for Ledger Live to ensure clear account separation.
## **Conclusion**

By understanding the differences in derivation paths and address generation between Ledger Live and Leather Wallet, you can manage your STX and BTC funds seamlessly. For Stacks, always use Leather to generate addresses, and for Bitcoin, exercise caution with Taproot addresses.

If you have further questions, feel free to reach out to our support team or consult our [Derivation Path Explainer](https://leather.io/guides/wallet-derivation-paths).

leather.Title: Leather
leather.Body:
Leather is a Bitcoin wallet built to unlock new ways to earn, use, and secure your Bitcoin-based assets.

It’s self-custodial—meaning only you control your keys and funds—and open-source, so you can verify how everything works under the hood. With support for the Stacks Layer 2 and emerging Bitcoin protocols, Leather helps you interact with new app ecosystems while staying anchored to Bitcoin.

Leather supports:

- BTC and sBTC
- STX and SIP-10 tokens
- Ordinals and inscriptions
- BRC-20, Runes
- Stamps
- Liquid Stacking tokens like stSTX and LiSTX
You can send, receive, store, swap, delegate, stack and sign transactions across the Stacks and Bitcoin networks.

Leather is designed for users who want to earn yield on Bitcoin, use apps secured by Bitcoin, and own their financial future—without centralized custody.

leather.Sentence: Leather is a wallet crafted for earning yield within the Bitcoin ecosystem. We are fully open-source and non-custodial.

Leather is a fully open-source, self-custodial wallet for Bitcoin and Bitcoin-secured assets. It supports BTC, STX, Ordinals, BRC-20s, sBTC, and more—giving users full control of their funds and identity across apps, DeFi protocols, and marketplaces.

Whether you’re earning yield, connecting to apps, or managing your Bitcoin-native assets, Leather offers a secure, transparent, and intuitive experience across browser, mobile and desktop.

zest.Title: Zest Protocol
zest.Body:
Zest Protocol is a decentralized borrowing and lending protocol built on Stacks, enabling users to earn yield or access liquidity using Bitcoin-backed assets. The protocol offers two core markets: the Stacks Market (live) and the Bitcoin Market (coming soon). It is designed with a strong emphasis on Bitcoin-native principles, using Clarity smart contracts and integrations that prioritize Bitcoin’s security and decentralization.

## Borrowing Overview

Zest Protocol Borrow enables overcollateralized borrowing using sBTC and other supported tokens. Users can lend or borrow directly through the Stacks Market, which operates in a non-custodial and permissionless way. The system draws inspiration from Aave v3 and supports perpetual borrowing terms, isolation mode for collateral management, and two borrowing types: traditional borrowing and E-Mode (efficiency mode).

### Traditional Borrowing

Users supply assets like stSTX, STX, or aeUSDC, which may be eligible as collateral (indicated in the app UI). Once collateral is supplied, users can borrow up to 50% LTV, with liquidation occurring if LTV reaches 70% (plus a 10% penalty). Collateral usage is currently limited to one asset at a time under isolation mode.

### E-Mode Borrowing

E-Mode allows borrowing up to 80% LTV when using highly correlated assets like STX and stSTX. Liquidation occurs at 85% LTV with a reduced 5% penalty. E-Mode must be manually activated in the interface and only applies to designated collateral types.

## Liquidation

If a user’s LTV breaches the threshold, a liquidation event is triggered. Liquidators can repay the borrower’s loan and claim a portion of the collateral at a discount. Zest provides open documentation for setting up liquidation bots.

## Yield and Supplying Assets

Lenders earn continuously compounding yield by supplying assets to Zest. Rates are dynamic and based on the pool's utilization rate. The UI displays current APYs and borrowing interest rates, which adjust as supply/demand shifts.

## Oracles and Risk Management

Zest uses Pyth Network for price feeds with tight staleness limits (3 minutes) and confidence interval protections. Risk classification of assets follows three categories:

- Collateral assets (e.g. STX, stSTX, sBTC)
- Borrow-only assets (e.g. aeUSDC, USDA)
- E-Mode assets (deep liquidity & correlation)
## BTCz and BTC Yield

Zest Protocol Earn (now deprecated) allowed users to mint BTCz by staking BTC via Babylon. BTCz was a liquid SIP-10 token on Stacks, representing staked BTC. BTCz could be deposited and withdrawn using dual-chain wallets like Leather. It may return if native BTC staking becomes more widely supported.

## Bitcoin-Native Architecture

Zest is Bitcoin-native by design:

- Collateral and yield are BTC-based (e.g. sBTC, BTCz)
- Built entirely on Stacks L2, secured by Bitcoin
- Smart contracts can read Bitcoin state directly
- Uses no custodians or wrapped Ethereum tokens
- Supports self-custody and Clarity-based trust-minimized logic
This architecture allows users to unlock liquidity and earn yield on BTC without compromising Bitcoin’s core principles of decentralization, transparency, and sovereignty.

zest.Summary:
Zest Protocol is a decentralized, non-custodial liquidity platform built on the Stacks Layer 2 for Bitcoin. It enables users to borrow assets like stablecoins against overcollateralized positions (e.g. sBTC, stSTX), or earn yield by supplying collateral into lending markets. With its first implementation focused on the Stacks Market, Zest supports lending, borrowing, and liquidations directly on the Stacks blockchain using Clarity smart contracts. 

Zest is also home to BTCz, a yield-bearing Bitcoin token on Stacks minted by staking BTC via Babylon. BTCz supports DeFi integration, tokenization of staking positions, and future reward mechanisms. While BTCz is being phased out in favor of sBTC, Zest’s platform evolution continues to prioritize secure, composable, Bitcoin-backed utility on Stacks. All interactions are non-custodial and designed for users who want to put Bitcoin to work in a programmable way, while retaining strong security guarantees from Bitcoin Layer 1.

brotocol.Title: Brotocol
brotocol.Body:
## What is Brotocol?

Brotocol is a Bitcoin-native DeFi platform that unifies Bitcoin liquidity with broader crypto ecosystems. It includes key apps like BroBridge (a BTC-to-aBTC bridge on Stacks) and **BroSwap** (a decentralized exchange for Bitcoin-linked assets). By converting BTC into aBTC, users can interact with DeFi tools while maintaining exposure to Bitcoin’s value and security.

Originally built with infrastructure from AlexLab and now expanded into its own system, Brotocol is operated through a decentralized validator network. It brings transparency, composability, and cross-chain functionality to the Bitcoin ecosystem.

### What You Can Do with Brotocol

- Bridge BTC into DeFi: Use BroBridge to convert BTC into aBTC on the Stacks chain.  
- Swap Bitcoin-based assets: Trade tokens like aBTC, STX, ALEX, TRIO, and others using BroSwap.  
- Monitor live usage: View the Explorer to track bridge and swap transactions.  
- Track reserves and security: Transparency is enforced through CoinFabrik-audited validator endpoints and publicly viewable reserves.
### Using Brotocol with Leather

Users can connect their Leather wallet to Brotocol’s apps (like BroBridge and BroSwap) using the Leather API. This enables secure Bitcoin and Stacks wallet integration for bridging, swapping, and interacting with DeFi tools without leaving the Brotocol interface.

### What's Next for Brotocol?

Brotocol is expanding to include:

- BroPay – A Bitcoin-native payment app (coming soon)  
- Multi-chain support for Base, Arbitrum, BNB, and Solana  
- Ongoing validator updates and new farming incentives

Users can connect their Leather wallet to Brotocol’s apps via the Leather API to bridge and trade securely. The platform uses validator governance and CoinFabrik-audited infrastructure to enable transparent, composable DeFi for Bitcoin users.

velar.Title: Velar
velar.Body:
Velar is a decentralized liquidity protocol built on the Bitcoin Layer 2 ecosystem, offering a full suite of DeFi products—including token swaps, perpetual futures, yield farming, and a token launchpad—accessible directly from the Bitcoin network through Stacks.

## How does Velar work?

At its core, Velar is designed to bring capital efficiency and composability to Bitcoin. Users can trade tokens with minimal fees through Dharma (Velar's native swap module), gain leveraged exposure to crypto markets using Artha (a perpetual DEX), or invest in early-stage Bitcoin projects via the Velar Launchpad. Each of these products is built to integrate deeply with the Bitcoin economy by leveraging Layer 2 infrastructure and secure smart contracts.

## Key features

Velar is Bitcoin-native in multiple ways. First, it integrates with Stacks, a Bitcoin Layer 2 that allows smart contracts to be secured by Bitcoin’s finality. This means users can interact with Velar apps and earn or swap using STX, sBTC, and other SIP-10 tokens, with all actions settled on Bitcoin. Second, Velar supports seamless cross-chain functionality with Ethereum through Velar Bridge, enabling asset movement between chains without needing custodial intermediaries.

The protocol is supported by a developer platform that includes APIs, an SDK, and contract audits to foster integrations and expand Bitcoin DeFi tooling. Velar is governed by its native token, used for rewards, governance, and potentially collateral in trading applications.

Users can interact with Velar using wallets like Leather, and participate in liquidity provision, trade STX or sBTC pairs, or gain leveraged exposure to assets like BTC or USDh on Velar's perpetuals exchange.

With the rise of sBTC and Bitcoin-based liquidity protocols, Velar positions itself as a gateway to composable, scalable, and user-friendly Bitcoin DeFi.
velar.Question: What is Velar?
velar.Prompt: Swap Bitcoin and STX, trade perpetuals, or explore IDOs by connecting your wallet to Velar on Stacks.
velar.Sentence: A DeFi suite offering trading, liquidity, and launchpad access built on Bitcoin L2s like Stacks
velar.Summary:
Velar is a DeFi protocol offering token swaps, leveraged trading, and launchpad access on Bitcoin Layer 2s like Stacks. It supports Bitcoin-native assets including sBTC and connects users to liquidity, staking, and cross-chain bridging.

With features like Dharma DEX, Artha Perpdex, and the Velar Launchpad, Velar delivers a full-spectrum trading and investment experience secured by Bitcoin. Its developer SDK and institutional backing reinforce its position as a premier DeFi platform on Stacks.

stacking-dao.Title: Stacking DAO
stacking-dao.Body:
Stacking DAO is a Stacking infrastructure for the Stacks Bitcoin L2. 

The protocol currently offers three services:

- **stSTX**: A liquid representation of stacked STX that accrues in value in STX as Stacking rewards are auto-compounded daily. It can also be used across DeFi to earn additional yield and points.
- **stSTXbtc**: A liquid stacking token backed 1-to-1 with STX, and holders receive sBTC rewards daily that can be claimed at any moment. stSTXbtc can also be used across Stacks dApps.
- **Native Stacking:** Delegate STX and earn BTC rewards with zero fees while STX are locked during the two-week Stacking cycles.
Security is a foundational aspect of Stacking DAO, which uses a decentralized signer set composed of over 10 trusted validators and has undergone six security audits from firms such as Clarity Alliance, CoinFabrik, and Immunefi. 

The platform currently boasts over $66 million in total value locked, with tens of thousands of active users taking advantage of flexible and secure Stacking opportunities.

## **Interacting with Stacking DAO in Leather**

Leather supports full stSTX and stSTXbtc visibility and app connectivity. You can:

- View your balances and accrued rewards
- Access external apps that integrate with Stacking DAO
This makes it easy to earn BTC from your STX while keeping your assets liquid and usable.
stacking-dao.Question: What is Stacking DAO?
stacking-dao.Prompt: Start earning BTC yield with Stacking by choosing between native, liquid, or sBTC-denominated options—fully integrated with Leather.
stacking-dao.Sentence: Stacking infrastructure offering native and liquid options with BTC and STX-based yield
stacking-dao.Data point instructions: Retrieve the most recently displayed total value locked (TVL) in USD from the homepage of stackingdao.com
stacking-dao.Summary:
Stacking DAO is the infrastructure layer for Stacking on Stacks, providing flexible ways for users to earn Bitcoin-based rewards. It supports native Stacking, where STX is locked in cycles and BTC yield is streamed directly to wallets, as well as liquid Stacking via stSTX and stSTXbtc—yield-bearing tokens that allow users to remain liquid and use their assets across DeFi protocols.

stSTX earns auto-compounding STX rewards, while stSTXbtc distributes sBTC rewards, offering two distinct approaches to earning yield. These assets can be used in DeFi apps like Zest Protocol, Bitflow, Velar, and Hermetica. With over $66 million in total value locked and a decentralized signer set, Stacking DAO is a key platform for accessing secure, flexible, and yield-generating Bitcoin opportunities on the Stacks blockchain.
stacking-dao.Disclaimer:
Leather does not operate or control Stacking DAO. Users should conduct their own research and use caution before interacting with third-party protocols.

BTC rewards and redemption mechanics may vary. Review Stacking DAO's terms and smart contract behavior before participating.

bitflow.Title: Bitflow
bitflow.Body:
## What is Bitflow?

Bitflow is a decentralized exchange (DEX) and liquidity aggregator built on Stacks, designed for Bitcoin-native traders. It enables seamless, non-custodial swaps across tokens, stablecoins, and Runes assets by routing trades through protocols like ALEX, Velar, and Arkadiko. Users can deposit assets like BTC, sBTC, USDA, or stSTX to earn real yield, optimize trade routes, and interact with innovative primitives such as Runes AMMs.

Bitflow’s routing engine identifies the best execution price across partner DEXs, giving traders the best possible swap outcomes. With low slippage, pooled liquidity, and deep integrations, Bitflow brings a high-performance DeFi experience to the Bitcoin ecosystem.

## Key Features

- DEX Aggregator: Bitflow sources liquidity from multiple Bitcoin-native DEXs to offer best-in-class execution prices.
- Cross-Asset Swaps: Swap BTC, SIP-10s, stablecoins, and Runes with full self-custody.
- Real Yield: Deposit BTC to earn BTC while putting capital to work in liquidity pools.
- Trade Optimization: Visualize different swap routes to maximize returns.
- Runes Integration: Earn and trade with Runes via Bitflow’s AMM.
## Bitflow and Leather

Leather integrates with Bitflow to give users a direct and seamless way to swap assets, earn yield, and access deep liquidity—all through their secure Bitcoin wallet.

- Trade Runes, SIP-10s, stablecoins, and sBTC
- Earn BTC through liquidity provisioning
- Optimize swap paths using Bitflow’s aggregator
- Stay in full control with non-custodial execution
bitflow.Question: What is Bitflow?
bitflow.Prompt: Start earning Bitcoin yield with optimized swaps and pooled liquidity by accessing Bitflow directly in Leather.
bitflow.Sentence: A Bitcoin-native DEX aggregator and liquidity hub that sources the best prices across Stacks-based protocols.
bitflow.Summary:
Bitflow is a decentralized exchange (DEX) and liquidity aggregator built on Stacks that helps users earn real Bitcoin yield through optimized trading and pooled liquidity. It connects to protocols like ALEX, Velar, and Arkadiko to deliver best-execution swaps and DeFi strategies with full self-custody.

Users can access Bitflow directly in Leather to swap, deposit, and earn yield on BTC, sBTC, stSTX, USDA, and more—all without giving up ownership of their assets.

alex.Title: ALEX
alex.Body:
ALEX is a Bitcoin-secured DeFi platform built on Stacks that delivers a full suite of financial tools for trading, lending, staking, and launching tokens. It combines on-chain smart contracts, low-fee swaps, and cross-chain liquidity to offer users a secure and accessible entry into decentralized finance.

## What users can do on ALEX

- Swap tokens: Use the ALEX AMM to swap SIP-10 assets like STX, ALEX, USDA, and others.
- Provide liquidity: Join pools and earn trading fees and rewards.
- Liquid stake: Stake ALEX tokens or other supported assets and receive liquid staking derivatives.
- Launch or buy tokens: Access IDOs through the multichain launchpad or list new assets with self-service tools.
- Bridge assets: Use the ALEX bridge, powered by Brotocol, to move tokens between Stacks, Ethereum, and Bitcoin-compatible networks.
## ALEX and Leather

Through Leather, users can directly:

- Trade supported tokens
- View DeFi yields and staking options
- Interact with ALEX’s smart contracts
- Track liquidity positions
ALEX is governed by the ALEX Lab Foundation and is supported by major Bitcoin ecosystem investors. With nearly $2.7B in total value bridged and over 70,000 unique wallets, ALEX is a key pillar of Bitcoin DeFi. Its infrastructure is anchored in Bitcoin finality, making it a powerful platform for builders and users alike.
alex.Question: What is ALEX?
alex.Prompt: Access Bitcoin-secured DeFi features like swaps, staking, lending, and launchpad tools on ALEX—available directly in Leather.
alex.Sentence: A DeFi platform on Stacks offering swaps, staking, fixed-term lending, and cross-chain liquidity with Bitcoin security
alex.Summary:
ALEX is a comprehensive decentralized finance protocol built on the Stacks blockchain, designed to bring advanced DeFi capabilities to Bitcoin. Through its platform, users can swap assets, provide liquidity, access fixed-yield lending, stake tokens, and participate in token launches—all secured by Bitcoin finality via Stacks.

ALEX supports a wide DeFi ecosystem, including a native AMM DEX, a bridge for multi-chain transfers, manual and liquid staking options, and a multichain launchpad. Its integration with Leather enables users to interact with these services seamlessly from a Bitcoin-native wallet, unlocking programmable financial utility without leaving the Bitcoin ecosystem.
alex.Disclaimer: ALEX is a third-party DeFi protocol not operated by Leather, and users should do their own research before interacting with it through the Leather wallet.

unpacking-leather-s-new-brand-identity.Title: Unpacking Leather's New Brand Identity
unpacking-leather-s-new-brand-identity.Body:
Today, we introduced Leather – a new Bitcoin wallet brand bringing Bitcoin to the rest of us. 

It is the Bitcoin wallet for users who want to tap into an emerging Bitcoin economy built on trustless and decentralized technologies. We believe in making Bitcoin Web3 a welcome place where everyone feels empowered to decide when – and how – to use their assets.

To go with our new brand, we’re also launching a whole new brand identity that emphasizes three key components to our mission: 

- Making Web3 wallets more accessible and less intimidating
- Breathing life into Bitcoin and establish it as the bedrock of Web3
- Building a Bitcoin wallet that feels tangible and long-lasting
We created Leather (formerly “Hiro Wallet”) to give Bitcoin users an avenue to put their BTC to work so that they, too, could access the growing Web3 ecosystem. Not only that, they could do so with a self-custodied wallet that gave them full control over their own Bitcoin-secured assets and online identity. 

That sense of welcome familiarity and personalization is embodied in the name, Leather, itself. Much like a classic, trustworthy physical leather wallet from the Web2 world, we want Leather to bring that same sense of tangibility and reliability into the Web3 experience. 

For the launch of our new brand, we collaborated with [Porto Rocha](https://portorocha.com/), a premier New York-based branding agency that has consistently pushed the boundaries with their forward-thinking designs. They have worked with some of the world’s most recognizable brands, and we were thrilled to have them on board to create a unique, distinct brand identity that aligned with our mission. 

We’re excited to introduce you to Leather. Let’s dive in.

## Here’s What’s New

Inspired by our commitment to building a Bitcoin wallet that can stand the test of time, our brand identity speaks to the accessibility, reliability and long-term value of Leather. 

### Our slogan

Bitcoin for the rest of us. 

Our new slogan is more than just a catchphrase; it’s a nod to our vision of making Bitcoin and Bitcoin Web3 a space that is easy to navigate for both new and experienced crypto users alike. Everyone should feel empowered to explore all the potential use cases being built on Bitcoin.

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/f725d1c5c0a8a239998d998a7bf7ad71.png)

### Wordmark

The Leather wordmark has been designed with a cursive typeface to speak to the timelessness and stability Leather users can expect to have with their wallet. It feels dynamic, digital and fluid, conveying Leather’s ease of use and our future-forward ethos.

### Our symbol

The looping “L” is a simple, yet distinguishable symbol that conveys the uniqueness of the Leather brand in the wider Web3 ecosystem.

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/659ce298505df8db1143848fe3cbf50c.gif)

### Color system

Our black and off-white color system gives users a sense of the precision and trust that comes with our brand. Designed to be compatible with both light and dark modes, this color system also furthers our user-friendly approach in ensuring that everything – down to the wallet’s visual display – is appealing in every respect.

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/2981c8d34de5c7ec49c0cf268e2b557c.png)

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/fa3a4946663b01ec04f9494fff4e25c5.png)

### Typography

Our primary typeface (Marché) is bold, confident, but also friendly to convey our dedication to being a leader in driving Bitcoin Web3 while also emphasizing the accessibility we want to give to users. Our secondary typeface (ABC Diatype) reflects the simple, yet utilitarian nature of our Leather apps.

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/528b9864883d658f0511934f38b29771.png)

### Illustrations

Our main illustration style consists of two distinct categories: technical illustrations and stickers.

Our technical illustrations represent the functionality of Leather. Our sticker illustrations add to the accessibility of our brand by showing a more colorful, fun side of Leather. Many of the stickers you see are also NFTs by artists in the Bitcoin ecosystem, creating opportunities for collaboration and community building around Bitcoin.

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/586d077e2e8ae7a4a99e325306b236a9.png)

![](https://leather-cms.s3.amazonaws.com/images/7c94d51c71dcb7a8a83961734dc77afb.png)

### Motion

Crypto and Web3 are ever evolving, and Leather is a Bitcoin wallet that moves to keep its users up to date with the latest developments on Bitcoin.

That’s why motion is a key component in much of our upcoming visual content. We want to convey to users that like Bitcoin Web3, we are dynamic, impactful and forward-thinking in what we build.

## Looking Ahead

Our new brand identity is, in many ways, a reflection of our long-term dedication to making Bitcoin Web3 a place where every user can participate in the revolutionary potential of Bitcoin. We want to be at the forefront of driving the global transition to a digital economy built on Bitcoin, the world’s oldest blockchain.

We believe that a Bitcoin wallet shouldn’t just be a user’s means to store their Bitcoin. It should be a tool that permits users to become active participants in the internet of tomorrow. 

That’s why Leather isn’t just a Bitcoin wallet. It’s Bitcoin for the rest of us.

*Connect to web3 applications built on Bitcoin with the *[Leather browser extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/leather/ldinpeekobnhjjdofggfgjlcehhmanlj)*. Install Leather – the only wallet you need to tap into the multilayered Bitcoin economy – today.*
